# conventions

| Rule                                                | Description                                                              | Default level |

| [allowed-directories](#allowed-directories)         | Only directories with these names may exist in some directories.         | `error`       |

| [export-name-pattern](#export-name-pattern)         | Exported names in matching files follow a pattern.                       | `error`       |
| [file-name-case](#file-name-case)                   | File names follow a naming case.                                         | `error`       |

| [forbidden-directories](#forbidden-directories)     | Directories with these names must not exist.                             | `error`       |
| [forbidden-files](#forbidden-files)                 | Files with these names must not exist.                                   | `error`       |
| [no-default-export](#no-default-export)             | Use named exports instead of default exports.                            | `error`       |

## allowed-directories

Only directories with these names may exist in some directories.

- **Id:** `conventions/allowed-directories`
- **Default level:** `error`

Each rule matches the parent directory by name, or by path when `directory` contains `/`,
and allows only directories whose names match `names` inside it, for example only
`components`, `hooks`, and `utils` in each feature. Deeper directories are not checked.

To fix a finding, rename the directory to an allowed name, or move its files into an
allowed directory. A singular name is reported with its allowed plural.

### Options

```ts
{
  rules: {
    directory: string;
    names: string[];
    message?: string;
    hint?: string;
  }[];
}
```

| Option              | Type       | Default  | Description                                                          |
| ------------------- | ---------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rules`             | `object[]` | required | Allowed names, each for a parent directory.                          |
| `rules[].directory` | `string`   | required | Name of the parent directory, or a path glob when it contains `/`.   |
| `rules[].names`     | `string[]` | required | Globs of the directory names allowed in the parent directory.        |
| `rules[].message`   | `string`   |          | Replaces the finding message, for example to say what to do instead. |
| `rules[].hint`      | `string`   |          | Shown under the finding as the next step.                            |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'conventions/allowed-directories': [
    'error',
    {
      rules: [
        {
          directory: 'src/features/*',
          names: [
            'components',
            'hooks',
            'models',
            'services',
            'utils',
            '__tests__',
          ],
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
},
```

## companion-files

Some files require a companion file, such as a test next to a component.

- **Id:** `conventions/companion-files`
- **Default level:** `error`

`requires` is a path relative to the file, where `{stem}` is the file name before the
first dot and `{name}` is the full name. It may be a glob, for example
`{stem}.{test,spec}.tsx`. Test files are never required to have companions.

To fix a finding, create the companion file.

### Options

```ts
{
  rules: {
    files: string | string[];
    requires: string;
    message?: string;
    hint?: string;
  }[];
}
```

| Option             | Type                 | Default  | Description                                                              |
| ------------------ | -------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `rules`            | `object[]`           | required | Companion rules.                                                         |
| `rules[].files`    | `string \| string[]` | required | Globs of files that need a companion.                                    |
| `rules[].requires` | `string`             | required | Path of the companion, relative to the file, with `{stem}` and `{name}`. |
| `rules[].message`  | `string`             |          | Replaces the finding message, for example to say what to do instead.     |
| `rules[].hint`     | `string`             |          | Shown under the finding as the next step.                                |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'conventions/companion-files': [
    'error',
    {
      rules: [
        { files: 'src/**/components/*.tsx', requires: '{stem}.test.tsx' },
      ],
    },
  ],
},
```

## directory-case

Directory names follow a naming case.

- **Id:** `conventions/directory-case`
- **Default level:** `error`

Directory names must follow one of the configured cases. Names like `__tests__` and
dot directories are ignored by default.

### Options

```ts
{
  case: Case | Case[];
  ignore?: string[];
}
```

| Option   | Type             | Default           | Description                               |
| -------- | ---------------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `case`   | `Case \| Case[]` | required          | Allowed cases. Suggestions use the first. |
| `ignore` | `string[]`       | `['__*__', '.*']` | Globs of names that are not checked.      |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'conventions/directory-case': ['error', { case: 'kebab' }],
},
```

## export-matches-filename

A file exports one value, named after the file.

- **Id:** `conventions/export-matches-filename`
- **Default level:** `error`

For example `dateUtil.ts` exports a `DateUtil` object and nothing else, so imports read
`DateUtil.format()` everywhere. Type exports are allowed. With `allowDeprecated`, other
values may stay while they are marked `@deprecated`, so consumers can migrate.
Scope the rule to the right files with an override.

To fix a finding, move the other exports into the main export, or into their own files.

### Options

```ts
{
  transform?: 'pascal' | 'camel' | 'none';
  allowDeprecated?: boolean;
}
```

| Option            | Type                            | Default    | Description                                                                                |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `transform`       | `'pascal' \| 'camel' \| 'none'` | `'pascal'` | How the file name becomes the export name: `dateUtil.ts` exports `DateUtil` with `pascal`. |
| `allowDeprecated` | `boolean`                       | `false`    | Allow other exports marked `@deprecated`.                                                  |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'conventions/export-matches-filename': [
    'error',
    { transform: 'pascal', allowDeprecated: true },
  ],
},
```

## export-name-pattern

Exported names in matching files follow a pattern.

- **Id:** `conventions/export-name-pattern`
- **Default level:** `error`

For example, exports from files in `hooks/` start with `use`. Patterns are globs matched
against each exported value name. Type exports and default exports are ignored.

### Options

```ts
{
  rules: {
    files: string | string[];
    pattern: string;
    message?: string;
  }[];
}
```

| Option            | Type                 | Default  | Description                                                          |
| ----------------- | -------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rules`           | `object[]`           | required | Name rules, each for a set of files.                                 |
| `rules[].files`   | `string \| string[]` | required | Globs of files whose exports are checked.                            |
| `rules[].pattern` | `string`             | required | Glob that each exported value name must match, such as `use*`.       |
| `rules[].message` | `string`             |          | Replaces the finding message, for example to say what to do instead. |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'conventions/export-name-pattern': [
    'error',
    { rules: [{ files: '**/hooks/*.ts', pattern: 'use*' }] },
  ],
},
```

## file-name-case

File names follow a naming case.

- **Id:** `conventions/file-name-case`
- **Default level:** `error`

The part of the file name before the first dot must follow one of the configured cases,
so `Button.test.tsx` is checked as `Button`. Use overrides for areas with other
conventions, for example PascalCase for components and camelCase for hooks.
Files named `index.*` and dotfiles are ignored by default.

### Options

```ts
{
  case: Case | Case[];
  ignore?: string[];
}
```

| Option   | Type             | Default             | Description                               |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `case`   | `Case \| Case[]` | required            | Allowed cases. Suggestions use the first. |
| `ignore` | `string[]`       | `['index.*', '.*']` | Globs of names that are not checked.      |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'conventions/file-name-case': [
    'error',
    { case: ['camel', 'pascal'], ignore: ['index.*', '.*', '*.md'] },
  ],
},
```

## file-name-pattern

Files in some directories must match a name pattern.

- **Id:** `conventions/file-name-pattern`
- **Default level:** `error`

Each rule matches the parent directory by name, or by path when `directory` contains `/`,
and requires file names in it to match `pattern`, for example `*Util.ts` in `utils`.
Test files are skipped unless `includeTests` is set.

### Options

```ts
{
  rules: {
    directory: string;
    pattern: string;
    message?: string;
    hint?: string;
  }[];
  includeTests?: boolean;
}
```

| Option              | Type       | Default  | Description                                                           |
| ------------------- | ---------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rules`             | `object[]` | required | Name rules, each for a directory.                                     |
| `rules[].directory` | `string`   | required | Name of the parent directory, or a path glob when it contains `/`.    |
| `rules[].pattern`   | `string`   | required | Glob that file names in the directory must match, such as `*Util.ts`. |
| `rules[].message`   | `string`   |          | Replaces the finding message, for example to say what to do instead.  |
| `rules[].hint`      | `string`   |          | Shown under the finding as the next step.                             |
| `includeTests`      | `boolean`  | `false`  | Also check test files.                                                |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'conventions/file-name-pattern': [
    'error',
    {
      rules: [
        { directory: 'utils', pattern: '*Util.ts' },
        {
          directory: 'hooks',
          pattern: 'use*.ts',
          message: 'Hooks start with use.',
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
},
```

## forbidden-directories

Directories with these names must not exist.

- **Id:** `conventions/forbidden-directories`
- **Default level:** `error`

Each pattern matches the directory name, or the path when it contains `/`. Give each
pattern a message that says what to do instead.

### Options

```ts
{
  patterns: {
    name: string;
    message?: string;
    hint?: string;
  }[];
}
```

| Option               | Type       | Default  | Description                                                          |
| -------------------- | ---------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `patterns`           | `object[]` | required | Forbidden directory names.                                           |
| `patterns[].name`    | `string`   | required | File or directory name glob, or a path glob when it contains `/`.    |
| `patterns[].message` | `string`   |          | Replaces the finding message, for example to say what to do instead. |
| `patterns[].hint`    | `string`   |          | Shown under the finding as the next step.                            |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'conventions/forbidden-directories': [
    'error',
    {
      patterns: [
        { name: 'helpers', message: 'Put helpers in utils/ instead.' },
      ],
    },
  ],
},
```

## forbidden-files

Files with these names must not exist.

- **Id:** `conventions/forbidden-files`
- **Default level:** `error`

Each pattern matches the file name, or the path when it contains `/`. Give each pattern
a message that says what to do instead, for example where the code belongs.

### Options

```ts
{
  patterns: {
    name: string;
    message?: string;
    hint?: string;
  }[];
}
```

| Option               | Type       | Default  | Description                                                          |
| -------------------- | ---------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `patterns`           | `object[]` | required | Forbidden file names.                                                |
| `patterns[].name`    | `string`   | required | File or directory name glob, or a path glob when it contains `/`.    |
| `patterns[].message` | `string`   |          | Replaces the finding message, for example to say what to do instead. |
| `patterns[].hint`    | `string`   |          | Shown under the finding as the next step.                            |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'conventions/forbidden-files': [
    'error',
    {
      patterns: [
        {
          name: 'helpers.ts',
```

## no-default-export

Use named exports instead of default exports.

- **Id:** `conventions/no-default-export`
- **Default level:** `error`

Named exports keep names consistent across imports and make re-exports and refactors
reliable. Allow default exports where a tool needs them, such as config files or stories,
with an override that turns this rule off for those files.

To fix a finding, export the value by name and update the imports.

### Options

None.

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'conventions/no-default-export': 'error',
},
```

## no-suppressions

No comments that switch off type checks, lint rules, or coverage.

- **Id:** `conventions/no-suppressions`
- **Default level:** `error`

Suppression comments hide problems instead of fixing them. Agents in particular tend to
add them to make a check pass. The rule reads the comments of source files and finds
directives such as `@ts-ignore`, `eslint-disable`, `oxlint-disable`, `biome-ignore`, and
coverage ignores at the start of a comment line. Text in strings is not a comment and is
never reported. Allow specific directives with `allow`.

To fix a finding, fix the underlying problem and remove the comment.

### Options

```ts
{
  directives?: string[];
  allow?: string[];
}
```

| Option       | Type       | Default                                                                                                                                              | Description                                              |
| ------------ | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `directives` | `string[]` | `['@ts-ignore', '@ts-expect-error', '@ts-nocheck', 'eslint-disable', 'oxlint-disable', 'biome-ignore', 'istanbul ignore', 'c8 ignore', 'v8 ignore']` | Directives to find in comments.                          |
| `allow`      | `string[]` | `[]`                                                                                                                                                 | Directives that are allowed, such as `@ts-expect-error`. |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'conventions/no-suppressions': ['error', { allow: ['@ts-expect-error'] }],
},
```

## required-files

Files that must exist in each element or matching directory.

- **Id:** `conventions/required-files`
- **Default level:** `error`

Each entry names where (`in`: an element type, or `{ directories: glob }`) and which
file must exist there (`path`, relative, may be a glob such as `index.{ts,tsx}`).

To fix a finding, create the file.

### Options

```ts
{
  files: {
    in: string | { directories: string };
    path: string;
    message?: string;
    hint?: string;
  }[];
}
```

| Option            | Type                                | Default  | Description                                                                |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `files`           | `object[]`                          | required | Required files.                                                            |
| `files[].in`      | `string \| { directories: string }` | required | An element type, or `{ directories }` for matching directories.            |
| `files[].path`    | `string`                            | required | File that must exist, relative to the element or directory. May be a glob. |
| `files[].message` | `string`                            |          | Replaces the finding message, for example to say what to do instead.       |
| `files[].hint`    | `string`                            |          | Shown under the finding as the next step.                                  |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'conventions/required-files': [
    'error',
    {
      files: [
        { in: 'feature', path: 'index.{ts,tsx}' },
        { in: { directories: 'src/**/components/*' }, path: '*.stories.tsx' },
      ],
    },
  ],
},
```

## root-only-files

Some files may only exist at the root of an element.

- **Id:** `conventions/root-only-files`
- **Default level:** `error`

Files such as barrels (`index.ts`) or message catalogs belong at the root of an element,
so each element has one of them. Names are globs matched against the file name.

To fix a finding, merge the file into the one at the element root.

### Options

```ts
{
  names: string[];
}
```

| Option  | Type       | Default  | Description                                                        |
| ------- | ---------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `names` | `string[]` | required | Globs of file names that may only exist at the root of an element. |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'conventions/root-only-files': [
    'error',
    { names: ['index.ts', 'messages.ts'] },
  ],
},
```

## Types

Types used by the options above.

### Case

A naming case: `kebab-case`, `camelCase`, `PascalCase`, or `snake_case`.

```ts
type Case = 'kebab' | 'camel' | 'pascal' | 'snake';
```
